newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips revamp continues with cable sale.
newsitem.headline: Philips revamp continues with cable sale.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said Tuesday it agreed to sell its stake in a cable television venture to partner United International Holdings Inc. of Colorado for about 800 million guilders ($425 million).

As part of the cash-and-stock deal, the venture, United and Philips Communications BV (UPC), will buy 3.17 million shares of United International from Philips, the Dutch electronics giant said in a statement said.
UPC is Europe's largest private cable operator. Including its investments in other ventures it serves more than 1.3 million subscribers, Philips said.

"This transaction enables us to fully capitalise on multi-channel television and other communication assets we have systematically put in place in 14 countries throughout Europe and in Israel," United International Chairman Gene Schneider said.
Philips, which recently reported its first net loss since 1992, said the sale was the latest step aimed at focusing on its core businesses.

"As is widely known, Philips is currently reviewing its portfolio of activities. As a result, the company has concluded that its cable TV operation is not a core activity," said Richard de Lange, president of Philips Media.

A Philips spokesman said the deal was expected to be completed in the third quarter but declined to say how Philips planned to use the proceeds. The sale is the latest since new chairman Cor Boonstra vowed in October to tackle struggling or underperforming operations.

Philips is restructuring to weed out non-core businesses and trim management ranks in a bid to boost profits. It is selling off units such as its Videoland and Superclub home entertainment businesses.
In addition, Philips said last month it would no longer fully subsidise losses at Grundig, its troubled German consumer electronics unit.
Analysts welcomed the move, which they said indicated that Boonstra meant business.

"There's more (restructuring) to come but maybe not as much as we've seen in the last three or four months," said Joost van Beek of Van Meer James Capel. "The largest of the bleeders have been attacked."
"At first glance it seems a fair price," said analyst Peter Wortel of Delta Lloyd Bank, adding it would help offset further restructuring costs he anticipated in 1997.
Philips said about 39 percent of the proceeds would be in the form of new securities issued by UPC, which Philips will sell once the deal is completed.
Philips makes a host of products, including light bulbs, semiconductors and appliances, and also owns the Polygram record label.
